modes.name: unbacked_promise
modes.definition: The reply tells the user what will happen next, or what a human will do, and neither a policy nor a tool result supports it.
modes.boundary: The route is right, but the reply promises an outcome nothing guarantees (e.g. 'will approve'). If the route itself is wrong, label wrong_resolution_route instead.

modes.name: wrong_resolution_route
modes.definition: The reply misstates, leaves out, or does not act on the resolution route the SPEC requires: automatic refund at or below the threshold, refund queued for human review above it, dispute within the dispute window, or escalation under ESC-1 to ESC-4 (offering a required handoff instead of making it counts as a failure).
modes.boundary: The agent takes or describes the wrong path (refund vs queue vs dispute vs refuse vs escalate) for the order's eligibility, window, or amount. A right path with an over-promised outcome is unbacked_promise. A status- or deadline-only reply that does not offer or describe a refund is a Pass.
modes.requirement: ESC-1 to ESC-4; facts.yaml refund_auto_approve_threshold_usd, dispute_window_days
modes.evaluator: llm_judge (plus code check on eligibility facts)

modes.name: unflagged_missing_or_inconsistent_data
modes.definition: The reply presents a value as known when the tool data is missing it, or treats tool data as reliable when it is ambiguous (several matches) or internally inconsistent, instead of saying so.
modes.boundary: The problem starts in the data (missing field, internal inconsistency, several matches) and the reply hides it or fills the gap. A reply that contradicts clean tool data is statement_conflicts_with_order_status.

modes.name: missing_policy_citation
modes.definition: The reply states a fact or rule that comes from a policy document (return or dispute window, refund threshold or auto-approval, refund timing, fee, cancellation rule) and does not name that policy's identifier in the same reply. A citation in an earlier turn does not count. Numbers that come from the user (such as a budget) or from order data (dates, totals, shipping time) are not policy claims.
modes.boundary: The claim is backed by a policy but the reply does not name its identifier. If no policy backs the claim, label unbacked_promise. A policy fact repeated from a tool result (e.g. the issue_refund note '5 to 10 business days') still needs the identifier.
modes.evaluator: code_check (policy number or rule in reply without a cw-/store- identifier)
